commit.message:
Never leave a leg with no swap: the runner lost half its RAM too

Run 32947239873 inverted the previous failure instead of fixing it.
linux-arm64 reached the swap step with 40G free, got an 8G swapfile and built
successfully. macos-arm64 reached it with 32G free, and 32 - 32 = 0 meant no
swapfile at all; it then went silent compiling media/libaom and was killed 42
minutes later with "The runner has received a shutdown signal". windows-x86_64
had 33G and likewise got nothing.

The reserve was calibrated as though disk were the whole problem. It is not.
The August 2026 runner rebuild shrank BOTH dimensions:

  disk  145G -> 72G   (114G free after cleanup -> 41G, and 32-33G by the time
                       the source tree and toolchains are unpacked)
  RAM    16G ->  8G   (measured this run: `Mem: 7.8Gi`)

So swap matters more now than it did when the old hardcoded 30G was written,
not less, and reserving disk by starving it trades a fast, self-describing
failure for a silent one: a thrashed runner is killed with no log after ~40
idle minutes, while running out of disk fails in twenty and names the file it
could not write.

Reserve 24G for the build, cap swap at 12G, and put a floor of 8G under it --
8G because that is precisely what linux-arm64 completed a full build on in the
same run. Every leg now gets at least what the one surviving leg had:

  40G free -> 12G swap, 28G build      33G free -> 9G swap, 24G build
  41G free -> 12G swap, 29G build      32G free -> 8G swap, 24G build

Also add a "Report resource headroom" step that runs on always(), so a failed
or killed leg still prints df/free afterwards. Whatever is left is what the
build did not need, which is the only honest input for this split. I have now
guessed these budgets twice and been wrong twice; the next adjustment should
read numbers instead.

Parallelism deliberately left alone. linux-arm64 built at the default -j with
8G of swap, so swap is the variable that separated success from failure this
run, and changing two at once would tell us nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

releases.name: v152.0.4-beta.27
releases.body:
> [!WARNING]
> Keep in mind that Camoufox is in active development and may not be suitable for a production environment.
> If you experience any issues, please report them [here](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues).

I've gone ahead and marked this release as the new latest stable due to the FF135 build being terribly out of date and unsuitable for modern anti-bot systems. If you were following the official/prerelease channel, please switch over to official/stable to fetch this release. You can always [pin the active version](https://camoufox.com/python/installation/#managing-multiple-camoufox-versions) the library launches to go back to the March 2025 FF135 build. 

## What's Changed
* fix: page-recycle hang under spoofed window dims (#666), + the unmerged pythonlib/settings halves of #637-#647 by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/673
    * Fixes `new_page()` hanging when window.outer* is spoofed
    * Fixes WebRTC proxy IP leak that was incomplete in beta.26
* Fix getResponseBody on ORB-decompressed responses by @pratyush618 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/671

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/compare/v152.0.4-beta.26...v152.0.4-beta.27

This release includes Windows 64-bit and 32-bit. Note that 32-bit releases may be removed in later versions and aren't thoroughly tested.

releases.name: v152.0.4-beta.26
releases.body:
## How to use prerelease builds

To use this release, follow the `official/prerelease` channel:

```bash
> camoufox set official/prerelease
> camoufox fetch
```

## What's Changed

* Stealth patches by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/666
    * Stops your real IP from leaking when behind a proxy. Fakes a network candidate when none is available so nothing looks inconsistent
    * Fixes the proxy set via launch argument being silently ignored (an HTTPS setting was overriding it)
    * Makes CSS screen-size checks match the spoofed screen size, so the real window size doesn't leak
    * Makes CSS2 system-font keywords (menu, caption, etc.) resolve to match the spoofed platform
    * Stops synthetic mouse input from stalling under heavy load. Also improves file-picker reliability
    * Sends a single input event when inserting text into form fields
    * Fixes reloading of about:blank pages
    * Fixes 4 things Firefox 152 broke: screenshots, popup events, tap/touch, and closing popup windows
    * Makes the locale set via launch argument actually apply
    * Fixes detectable "tells" (headless mode, impossible screen geometry)
    * Fixes speech-voice spoofing so the host machine's real voices don't leak
* Fix uninitialized DateTimeInfo cache in worker timezone override by @pratyush618 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/669
* Add disableInstantAnimations opt-out flag by @pratyush618 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/667
* ci: fix build.yml on GitHub-hosted runners (source wipe, ccache, OOM) by @neuregex in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/662

### Python library
* Fix server launch on Playwright 1.60 by @pratyush618 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/670
* fix: kill Xvfb with SIGKILL and clean up X11 lock/socket files by @Praveensenpai in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/652
* Python library bumped to 0.5.3 and published to pypi

## New Contributors
* @Praveensenpai made their first contribution in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/652
* @pratyush618 made their first contribution in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/669
* @neuregex made their first contribution in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/662

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/compare/v152.0.2-alpha...v152.0.4-beta.26

---

> [!NOTE]
> A Windows 32-bit build is included in this release but may be excluded from future releases.

Symptom: After completing the Cloudflare “I’m human” checkbox, the site loads, but sending a chat message fails. Observed failure: POST https://grok.com/rest/app-chat/conversations/new returns HTTP 403 with JSON: { "error": { "code": 7, "message": "Request rejected by anti-bot rules.", "details": [] } } Extra: navigator.webdriver is false in Camoufox. Same machine/IP works fine in normal Chrome/Firefox. Screenshots: Screenshot shows Grok UI failing to respond and DevTools Network showing .../conversations/new returning 403 with anti-bot error. To Reproduce: Testing site: https://grok.com/ (login required). Run (minimal repro project): cd C:\code\camoufox_python_standalone.\run.cmd -ProfileId test_profile_grok -Url "https://grok.com/" -GeoIP -Humanize Script snippet / initialization: import camoufox.utils as cfx_utilsfrom camoufox.sync_api import Camoufoxfrom_options = cfx_utils.launch_options( os="windows", geoip=True, humanize=True, headless=False, proxy=None,)from_options["user_data_dir"] = r"C:\code\camoufox_python_standalone\profiles\test_profile_grok\userdata"with Camoufox(from_options=from_options, persistent_context=True) as ctx: page = ctx.pages[0] if ctx.pages else ctx.new_page() page.goto("https://grok.com/", wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=60000) # Manual steps: login → pass Cloudflare checkbox → type a message → click Send # Then the API call /rest/app-chat/conversations/new returns 403 + code 7 Other questions: Are you using a proxy? issues.title: Detection status by site (tracking)
issues.body:
# Detection status by site

Tracking issue consolidating site-specific detection reports. Individual "site X blocks me" threads are merged here; **specific, reproducible leaks keep their own issues** (linked below) so they don't get buried.

## How to contribute a report

A detection report is only actionable with these four things:

1. **Date, and both versions** — `camoufox version` output (browser build *and* pip package)
2. **OS**, and headless / headful / virtual
3. Whether **stock Firefox via Playwright, same IP, same proxy** also fails
4. **The site**, and what specifically happens (block page, captcha loop, silent 403, HTTP status)

Point 3 is the one that matters most. Without it we cannot separate browser fingerprinting from IP or proxy reputation, and most reports stall there. Point 1 is what makes a report survive: the table below shows how much of the backlog aged out before anyone could act on it.

## Consolidated reports

Every row was an individual issue, now closed and merged here. "At report" is the version the reporter was actually running on that date — not the current tree.

| Site | Vendor / WAF | Reported | Browser at report | pip at report | Source | What the report actually shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *not named* | reporter's own targets | 2026-07-20 | `152.0.4-beta.28` | `cloverlabs 0.6.0` | #688 | **Proxy reputation, not fingerprint.** Clean IP passes; every proxy fails. Reporter states stock Firefox is also detected, so there is no browser delta here. One commenter reports beta.27 working — worth a bisect if anyone can confirm. |
| realtor.com | Kasada | 2026-02-01 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | `0.4.11` | #476 | Reporter attributes it to a TLS fingerprint difference from stock Firefox. If correct, out of scope — see caveats. |
| grok.com | Cloudflare / x.ai | 2026-01-12 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | `0.4.11` | #455 | Challenge **passes** and the page loads; the subsequent `POST /rest/app-chat/conversations/new` fails. A post-challenge signal, not a page-load fingerprint. |
| *hCaptcha (general)* | hCaptcha | 2025-11-19 | not stated | not stated | #423 | Claims model definition files stopped being downloaded. Overlaps #733 — retest together. |
| facebook.com | `auth_platform` | 2025-11-18 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | not stated | #420 | No reproduction detail supplied. |
| discord.com | hCaptcha | 2025-10-22 | not stated | not stated | #406 | Private tab on the **same IP** passes. That isolates it to the browser — the most useful control in this table. Likely subsumed by #733. |
| google.com | — | 2025-09-14 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | not stated | #388 | 37 comments, no isolated signal. |
| camelcamelcamel.com | Cloudflare | 2025-05-19 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | `0.4.11` | #311 | **Container-only**: the same script and IP pass outside Docker. The repro also pins a v135 UA by hand, which is itself a signal — retest without it. |
| market.yandex.ru, ya.ru | Yandex SmartCaptcha | 2025-05-10 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | not stated | #300 | — |
| x.com | — | 2025-04-16 | not stated | `0.4.11` | #274 | Login flow returns "We blocked an attempt to access your account". |
| twitch.tv | — | 2025-04-05 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | `0.4.11` | #264 | "Your browser is not currently supported" reads as a UA or capability sniff rather than a fingerprint verdict — see #744 and #558. |
| pros.lacentrale.fr | DataDome | 2025-03-26 | `135.0.1-beta.24` | not stated | #258 | Fails without a proxy too, so not IP reputation. |

### What this table says

**Ten of the twelve reports were filed against `135.0.1-beta.24`.** The tree is now on `152.0.4-beta.30`. None of those rows can be acted on as filed — they describe a browser that is roughly seventeen releases behind, and a stale Firefox base is the single most common cause of detection reports. They are kept here as history, not as an open queue.

Of the two filed against a current build, #688 measures proxy reputation rather than the browser.

**If you are hitting one of these sites today, please open a fresh report against the current build** rather than commenting on this issue. A new report on `152.x` with point 3 answered is worth more than all twelve rows above.

## Actionable leaks — tracked separately, not merged here

These have identified causes and are fixable independently of any particular site:

- **#733** — Playwright globals reachable on `window` in the page's main world; measured against hCaptcha token acceptance. Needs re-measurement on `152.0.4-beta.30`, since #745 reworked main-world init scripts after it was filed. Most likely explanation for the hCaptcha rows above.
- **#744** — UA / browser version mismatch flagged by browserscan. Related: #753 (`navigator.appVersion` leaks the host OS on the preset path).
- **#558** — `canPlayType()` / `isTypeSupported()` leak system codec libraries. **PR #562 is queued for the next build.**
- **#271** — PerimeterX and DataDome detect when `page.route` is used. The only report here that names a *trigger* rather than a site, which makes it the one worth working. Related: #428.
- **#577** — favicon supercookie. `camoufox.cfg:338` disables `privacy.partition.network_state`, which is the mitigation. Needs a concrete measurement against Camoufox before it is actionable.
- **#222** — timezone / Accept-Language mismatch.

## Standing caveats

- A stale Firefox base is the single most common cause of detection reports. The tree is now on **152.0.4-beta.30**; anything filed against 135 or 146 needs a retest before it means anything.
- An intercepting proxy (mitmproxy and similar) replaces the TLS fingerprint entirely and will get you detected regardless of browser — see #396.
- Manually overriding `navigator.userAgent` via `i_know_what_im_doing=True` creates a UA/engine mismatch that is itself a strong signal — see #353, #311.
- TLS/JA3 spoofing is out of scope (negotiated in NSS, below the spoofing layer) — see #358.
- Proxy reputation is not a browser bug. If a clean IP passes and your proxy does not, the browser is not what is being detected — see #688.

issues.title: Search service fails to initialize: bundled `search-config-overrides-v2` dump is missing `recordType`
issues.body:
## Summary

`SearchService.#init()` throws on every launch, on a clean profile, in both
`152.0.4-beta.28` and `152.0.4-beta.29`. The browser ends up with **no search
engines at all**, and — because the urlbar's heuristic result depends on the
search service — the address bar drop-down shows **nothing**: no history, no
autofill, no bookmarks. Typing a word navigates to it as a hostname instead.

## Error

```
console.debug: SearchService: "init"
console.error: SearchService: "#init: failure initializing search:"
    (new Error("reason: JSON error: missing field `recordType` at line 1 column 114",
     "moz-src:///toolkit/components/uniffi-bindgen-gecko-js/components/generated/RustSearch.sys.mjs", 2681))
```

## Cause

The bundled Remote Settings dump

```
omni.ja → defaults/settings/main/search-config-overrides-v2.json
```

holds one record whose keys are:

```
clickUrl, id, identifier, last_modified, partnerCode, schema, telemetrySuffix, urls
```

There is no `recordType`, which the Rust `SearchEngineSelector` requires. For
comparison, every one of the 157 records in the sibling `search-config-v2.json`
does carry `recordType`, so only the overrides dump is stale.

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
camoufox fetch official/152.0.4-beta.29
# fresh profile, search logging on
printf 'user_pref("browser.search.log", true);\n' > /tmp/prof/user.js
camoufox -profile /tmp/prof -headless -no-remote about:blank
```

The error appears within a second of startup. `search.json.mozlz4` is never
written, and the profile has no engines.

## Impact

- No search from the address bar; a typed word is treated as a hostname.
- The urlbar drop-down is empty — history and autofill are unreachable even
  though `places.sqlite` is populated and `browser.urlbar.suggest.history` is
  `true`. All urlbar providers register fine (`UrlbarProviderPlaces`,
  `UrlbarProviderAutofill`, `UrlbarProviderHeuristicFallback`); the results just
  never get built.
- Adding an engine through `policies.json` (`SearchEngines.Add`) does not help,
  and neither does a WebExtension declaring `chrome_settings_overrides.
  search_provider` — both register through the same dead service.

## Suggested fix

Refresh the bundled `search-config-overrides-v2.json` from Remote Settings so
its record carries `recordType`, or ship `{"data": []}` — the overrides
collection is optional, and an empty one lets the service start.

Locally, replacing that file inside `omni.ja` with `{"data": []}` is the only
workaround we found, and it is lost on every browser update.

## Environment

- Camoufox `152.0.4-beta.28` and `152.0.4-beta.29`, Windows x86_64
- Clean profile, no policies, no extensions

issues.title: 13 fingerprint setters are exposed to page script on window (callable, enumerable)
issues.body:
The `set*` fingerprint setters are declared in `dom/webidl/Window.webidl`, so they are members of the **Window interface** — present on the page's own `window`, enumerable, and callable by ordinary page script.

Measured on the shipped `152.0.4-beta.30` Linux x86_64 build.

## What a page sees

An inline `<script>` on a served page — i.e. what a *site* sees, not what automation sees:

```
visible to page: 13/14

['setFontSpacingSeed', 'setAudioFingerprintSeed', 'setTimezone', 'setScreenDimensions',
 'setScreenColorDepth', 'setNavigatorPlatform', 'setNavigatorOscpu',
 'setNavigatorHardwareConcurrency', 'setWebGLVendor', 'setWebGLRenderer', 'setFontList',
 'setSpeechVoices', 'setWebRTCIPv4']
```

Identical whether launched through the camoufox Python package or through raw Playwright.

They are not merely reachable by name:

```
typeof                   function
'setTimezone' in window  true
own_descriptor           {writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true}
getOwnPropertyNames      includes it
for...in over window     finds it
toString                 function setTimezone() { [native code] }
```

Because they are **enumerable own properties**, a generic "diff this window against a reference Firefox" script finds all 13 without knowing any of their names.

## They are also callable, and they work

```js
navigator.hardwareConcurrency            // 8
window.setNavigatorHardwareConcurrency(999)   // no throw
navigator.hardwareConcurrency            // 999
```

So a page can both detect camoufox with certainty and rewrite the values it is shown.

## Why the existing protection does not cover this

Two mechanisms are easy to conflate, and only one applies:

* **World isolation (#707)** hides JS that camoufox adds *inside its sandbox*. These setters are not injected JS — they are on the Window interface, which belongs to the page. Isolation cannot hide them, and never could.
* **The `Func=` guard plus `DisableFunction()` self-destruct** is the mechanism that is supposed to hide them. It only fires **when a setter is called**.

That is the gap. The normal Python flow applies the fingerprint through `CAMOU_CONFIG` in C++ and does not call these setters at all — `fingerprints.py` only emits a `setTimezone` call, and only when a timezone is explicit. Nothing calls them, so nothing self-destructs, so they stay on `window` for the page's whole lifetime.

Verified that the C++ path is sufficient on its own — raw Playwright, no Python layer, so no init script exists:

```
CAMOU_CONFIG timezone only  ->  page tz = Asia/Tokyo
```

## Two smaller defects found alongside

**`TimezoneManager::DisableFunction()` is never called.** It is defined correctly and does the `PutBool`, but nothing invokes it, unlike its siblings:

```
speech-voices-spoofing.patch   defines :65   called :171   OK
font-list-spoofing.patch       defines :73   called :182   OK
timezone-spoofing.patch        defines :54   never called  BUG
```

So `setTimezone` stays exposed even in the one flow that *does* call it — the `JS_DeleteProperty` in `SetTimezone` is futile, because the `Func=` guard still returns true and the WebIDL resolve hook re-adds the property.

**`setCanvasSeed` does not exist.** It is in build-tester's `SELF_DESTRUCT_FUNCTIONS` list but appears nowhere in `patches/` or `additions/`, so that check passes vacuously.

## Why build-tester reports this as healthy

build-tester scores 405/408 with only `selfDestruct.setTimezone` failing, which reads as "14 of 15 fine". That is an artifact of its own flow: it *calls every setter itself* to build per-context profiles, which triggers each `DisableFunction` before it checks. It is measuring a configuration real users do not run.

## Reproduction

Serve a page containing:

```html
<!doctype html><body><script>
  const S = ['setFontSpacingSeed','setAudioFingerprintSeed','setTimezone','setScreenDimensions',
             'setScreenColorDepth','setNavigatorPlatform','setNavigatorOscpu',
             'setNavigatorHardwareConcurrency','setWebGLVendor','setWebGLRenderer','setFontList',
             'setSpeechVoices','setWebRTCIPv4'];
  document.title = S.filter(n => typeof window[n] !== 'undefined').length + '/13 exposed';
</script></body>
```

then `page.goto(url)` and read `page.title()`. Reading via `page.evaluate()` will **not** show this correctly — that runs in the isolated world, which is the same blind spot as #738.

## Directions

Rather than making the self-destruct fire more reliably, it seems better not to expose these to content at all:

* **Chrome-gate them** — require a chrome/addon caller in the `Func=` guard, the way `shadow-root-bypass.patch` uses `Func="Document::IsCallerChromeOrAddon"`. Content never sees them regardless of whether they have been called. Needs checking that camoufox's own callers still qualify — the isolated-world sandbox holds an expanded principal, not a system principal.
* **Drop the content-facing API** where `CAMOU_CONFIG` already covers it, and use juggler's chrome-side `Browser.setTimezoneOverride` (`BrowserHandler.js:257`) for the per-context case.

The `DisableFunction` call is worth adding regardless, but on its own it fixes one symptom of the 13.

Happy to send a PR once there is a view on which direction is preferred — the chrome-gating change touches every manager, so it is worth agreeing the approach first.

issues.title: fingerprint_preset leaks the host OS through navigator.appVersion
issues.body:
### Describe the bug:

`from_preset()` sets `navigator.userAgent`, `navigator.platform` and `navigator.oscpu` from the captured device, but never `navigator.appVersion`. Firefox reports `appVersion` as `"5.0 (<OS token>)"`, so an unset value falls through to the **host's** own — and any page reading two properties sees them contradict each other.

Measured on `152.0.4-beta.29`, macOS host, headless, `geoip=False`:

| launch | `navigator.platform` | `navigator.appVersion` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `os="linux"` (generated) | `Linux x86_64` | `5.0 (X11)` |
| `os="windows"` (generated) | `Win32` | `5.0 (Windows)` |
| `os="macos"` (generated) | `MacIntel` | `5.0 (Macintosh)` |
| `os="linux", fingerprint_preset=True` | `Linux x86_64` | **`5.0 (Macintosh)`** ← the host |

The generated (browserforge) path is coherent on all three, which is why this only shows on the preset path.

The same launch, read together as a page would:

```
ua         : Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:152.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/152.0
oscpu      : Linux x86_64
platform   : Linux x86_64
appVersion : 5.0 (Macintosh)
```

`navigator.appVersion` is already declared in `settings/properties.json`, so nothing in the browser needs to change — only the Python layer never populates it.

### To Reproduce:

```python
import asyncio
from camoufox import AsyncCamoufox

async def main():
    async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True, os="linux", geoip=False,
                             fingerprint_preset=True) as browser:
        page = await browser.new_page()
        await page.set_content("<body></body>")
        print(await page.evaluate(
            "() => [navigator.platform, navigator.appVersion]"
        ))

asyncio.run(main())
```

On a macOS host this prints `['Linux x86_64', '5.0 (Macintosh)']`. On a Linux host, try `os="windows"`.

### Other questions:

1. Are you using a proxy? No — `geoip=False`, nothing network-dependent.
2. Is it random or every time? Every time, on every preset, because the value is never set.
3. What OS are you using? macOS host; the leak is the host's OS whatever that is.

### Version:

```
Browser   official/stable/152.0.4-beta.29
Camoufox  0.5.4 (also present at HEAD — `appVersion` appears nowhere in pythonlib/camoufox/fingerprints.py)
```

### Note

This may well be what #744 is seeing — that report is `fingerprint_preset=True` with `os='linux'` on a macOS host, which is exactly this configuration, and browserscan's "browser version mismatch" check reads `appVersion`. I could not confirm from the screenshot there, so I am filing this separately rather than assuming.

Happy to send a PR — I have a one-function fix and a regression test that fails without it.

issues.title: humanize: trajectory points at x==0 / y==0 still deadlock the global input chain (#225 fix covers only the far edges)
issues.body:
### Summary

The exact-edge bounds guard added in #680 (beta.28) fixes only the **far** edges
(`>= width`, `>= height`). The **near** edges are still let through, because the
check is `< 0` rather than `<= 0`:

```js
// PageHandler.js, humanize trajectory
if (currentX < 0 || currentY < 0 || currentX >= boundingBox.width || currentY >= boundingBox.height)
//   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ x==0 / y==0 pass                    ^^^^^^^^^^ fixed in #680
  continue;
```

A trajectory point at exactly `x == 0` or `y == 0` is dispatched, fires as an exit
event rather than `eMouseMove`, produces no `hit-renderer` ack, and wedges the
process-global activation chain — the same deadlock #225/#680 describe, just from
the opposite side of the viewport.

### Reproduction / evidence

Instrumented `PageHandler.js` (logging around `camouGetMouseTrajectory` and each
`sendOne`) on `v152.0.4-beta.28`, real site, cold start:

```
[HUMZ] traj-start from=(0,0) to=(667,302) box=1294x676.6
[HUMZ] traj-got n=114
[HUMZ] send i=2 (31,0)      <- y == 0; dispatched, no ack, never returns
```

No `ack` line follows. The click times out; every later input in that process hangs.

This also explains two symptoms that were confusing before:

- **The page observes zero `mousemove` events during the hang** — the point fired as
  an exit event, so a `mousemove` listener never sees it.
- **It clusters on the session's first pointer input.** `_lastTrackedPos` starts at
  `{x: 0, y: 0}` (`PageHandler.js:86`), so the first trajectory always departs from
  the top-left corner; with the +/-80px knot boundary from `MouseTrajectories.hpp`
  that reliably produces points on `x == 0` / `y == 0`. Once a move lands on an
  interior point, later trajectories never touch the near edges.

Cold-start hang rate on our workload: **1 in 3** before the change below,
**0 in 20** after.

### Suggested fix

Make the guard symmetric:

```js
if (currentX <= 0 || currentY <= 0 || currentX >= boundingBox.width || currentY >= boundingBox.height)
  continue;
```

`tests/patches/humanize-edge-deadlock.py` passes on beta.28 as-is because its
`EDGE_TARGETS` only probe the right/bottom edges. Adding a near-edge target (e.g.
`(1, 350)` / `(500, 1)`, or simply asserting the very first move of a session)
would have caught this.

Optionally, initialising `_lastTrackedPos` to an interior point (as
`coryking/camoufox` does with a random in-viewport position) would additionally
remove the systematic corner departure — though on that fork the guard is still
the older strict-`>` form, so both edges remain reachable there.

### Environment

- browser: `v152.0.4-beta.28` (verified identical humanize block in `v152.0.4-beta.30`)
- pythonlib: `0.5.4`
- headless, `humanize=True`

issues.title: Memory Increases with Long Running Tasks
issues.body:
### Describe the bug:

Memory increases observed when attempting to navigate to pages. I checked to make sure that caching wasn't enabled. Also switched to headless mode to ensure it didn't have something to do with the virtual display. When switching back to normal playwright using chromium, this behavior is not observed.

As an example, my device has 8GB of RAM. Started out with ~2GB used with Camoufox running.  After ~1-2 hrs of running, my device started using swap as RAM was full. Once it's completely out of memory and the browser crashes or I close the browser prematurely, memory restores back to normal levels.

I **love** this browser and would hate to have to resort back to using Chromium. But I'm currently unable to do long-running tasks with this behavior. 

Happy to try to help how I can to get this resolved!

In my head, this could be one of two things:
- There's a memory leak in the browser where something isn't getting freed properly when navigating 
- Navigating to pages caches info that is required even if "caching" is disabled. This is my current workaround while #224 is still open. 

### To Reproduce:

I believe this is something that can be tested just by doing an infinite loop of `goto()`s with a sleep:

1. Open a few browsers and note initial memory usage
2. Run `goto(...)` and sleep(1) in a loop
After running for awhile, come back and note new memory usage.

### Version:
v135.0.1-beta.24

Tried this also on beta.23 and experiencing the same behavior.

issues.title: Better humanization
issues.body:
Some ideas in no particular order:

Human like scrolling behavior when scrolling elements into view. Cursor points on the element it wants to scroll and scrolling is done via the mouse wheel, with some uncertainty (go down, go up, go down) stutter etc.

Move the mouse to random points sometimes, although now the mouse trajectory seems human like if it always moves from one action thing to another action thing it is suspicious. It needs a little ADHD.

Humans will also just park their cursor for a bit on a random part of the page.

Also when entering the "desired" element to click on, just wait a bit before clicking, maybe even go back outside the element before re-entering and then click.

Add a randomized delay between actions, e.g. wait between 1-4 seconds between filling form fields. We could even define what an action is and then make sure that we don't do more than x actions a minute. Do some bogus actions in between maybe.

For typing, add random delays between characters. Maybe even a more complex algo which takes the keyboard layout into account. Make some mistakes while typing, but correct them.

Actions like .focus should be done with a humanized mouse cursor. Same for selecting the value of a select element. This also applies to other things like there should always be a click before fill or type. (Or alternatively simultate the tab key to switch between fields sometimes)

Add tiny random delays between multiple clicks on the same element e.g. double click.

Occasional small mouse movement while "typing".

I can help with some of the low hanging fruit, I just would like some feedback on my ideas first. Did I accidentally request anything that's already implemented?

Basically what I want from humanize is to set it to true and then just write the most straight forward playwright code to achieve the goal, but when running it looks like a human did it. I don't want to think about clicks, delays, typing etc.

I would like to add two new parameters to the browser config `min_action_delay` and `max_action_delay`.

issues.title: canvas:seed is declared and passed through, but nothing consumes it
issues.body:
## Who's asking I maintain [camoufox-profile-manager](https://github.com/polyackiy/camoufox-profile-manager), an open-source, self-hosted profile manager built on Camoufox — roughly what AdsPower or Dolphin do commercially, for people who would rather run it themselves. Camoufox does the hard part; we manage profiles, proxies, groups and the browser lifecycle around it. Thanks for the browser. Pinning a resolved config and replaying it across launches works beautifully — user agent, screen, GPU, cores, audio and fonts all hold steady, which is exactly what a long-lived profile needs. **This is not a request to change any default.** We have a working setup and are not blocked. It is a report that one advertised property appears to be inert, in case that is news to you. ### Describe the bug: #### The finding `canvas:seed` is advertised as a config property but nothing seems to consume it: - Declared in `settings/properties.json` and `settings/camoucfg.jvv` - Generated and passed by `pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py` (`set_into(config, 'canvas:seed', randint(...))`) - Referenced by `tests/patches/config-overrides.py` - **Not read anywhere in `additions/camoucfg/MaskConfig.hpp`**, and no patch in `patches/` mentions canvas `audio:seed` and `fonts:spacing_seed` sit beside it in the same code paths and do take effect, which is what made this surprising. Setting `canvas:seed` to any value produces no change in the exported canvas. Relatedly, `docs/per-context-patches.md` documents `window.setCanvasSeed()`, but it is `undefined` in the shipped build while its siblings are defined: ``` window.setCanvasSeed undefined window.setNavigatorUserAgent function window.setWebGLVendor function ``` If that work simply is not released yet, this may already be handled on your side — a pointer is all we need. ### To Reproduce: Camoufox `152.0.4-beta.28`, Python lib 0.5.x, macOS arm64.
canvas_seed_repro.py ```python """Reproduction: canvas:seed does not affect the 2D canvas fingerprint. Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.28, Python lib 0.5.x. pip install camoufox[geoip] && camoufox fetch python canvas_seed_repro.py Every check below is printed with what was expected, so the output stands on its own. """ import asyncio import hashlib import tempfile from pathlib import Path from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox # A page reads its canvas the way a fingerprinting script would. CANVAS = """() => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 300; c.height = 70; const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.textBaseline = 'top'; x.font = '16px Arial'; x.fillStyle = '#f60'; x.fillRect(0, 0, 120, 25); x.fillStyle = '#069'; x.fillText('canvas probe', 2, 18); return c.toDataURL(); }""" SITE = "https://example.com" OTHER_SITE = "https://iana.org" def digest(value: str) -> str: return hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest()[:16] async def read_canvas(context, url=SITE): page = await context.new_page() await page.goto(url, wait_until="domcontentloaded", timeout=45000) value = digest(await page.evaluate(CANVAS)) await page.close() return value async def main(): root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="canvas-seed-")) seed_config = {"canvas:seed": 424242} def options(profile_dir): return dict( headless=True, os="windows", i_know_what_im_doing=True, persistent_context=True, user_data_dir=str(root / profile_dir), config=dict(seed_config), ) print("Camoufox canvas:seed reproduction") print("=" * 66) # 1. Within one session the value is stable per site. This is correct. async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: first_tab = await read_canvas(context) second_tab = await read_canvas(context) other_site = await read_canvas(context, OTHER_SITE) print("\nWithin one session, canvas:seed = 424242") print(f" same site, tab 1 {first_tab}") print(f" same site, tab 2 {second_tab} equal: {first_tab == second_tab} (expected: equal)") print(f" a different site {other_site} equal: {first_tab == other_site} (expected: not equal)") # 2. Across launches of the SAME profile with the SAME seed, it changes. # This is the bug: the seed should make it reproducible. async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: second_launch = await read_canvas(context) async with AsyncCamoufox(**options("a")) as context: third_launch = await read_canvas(context) print("\nSame profile, same seed, relaunched") print(f" launch 1 {first_tab}") print(f" launch 2 {second_launch}") print(f" launch 3 {third_launch}") stable = first_tab == second_launch == third_launch print(f" all equal: {stable} (expected: equal, since the seed is fixed)") # 3. Two different seeds, fresh profiles: no relationship either way. async with AsyncCamoufox(**{**options("b"), "config": {"canvas:seed": 111}}) as context: seed_111 = await read_canvas(context) async with AsyncCamoufox(**{**options("c"), "config": {"canvas:seed": 999}}) as context: seed_999 = await read_canvas(context) print("\nDifferent seeds, fresh profiles") print(f" canvas:seed = 111 {seed_111}") print(f" canvas:seed = 999 {seed_999}") # 4. Is the per-context API from docs/per-context-patches.md present? async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=True, os="windows", i_know_what_im_doing=True) as browser: page = await browser.new_page() await page.goto("about:blank") present = await page.evaluate( """() => ({ setCanvasSeed: typeof window.setCanvasSeed, setNavigatorUserAgent: typeof window.setNavigatorUserAgent, setWebGLVendor: typeof window.setWebGLVendor, })""" ) print("\nPer-context API in this build") for name, kind in present.items(): print(f" window.{name:24} {kind}") print("\n" + "=" * 66) print("Result:", "seed is honoured" if stable else "the seed has no effect on the canvas fingerprint") asyncio.run(main()) ```
``` Within one session, canvas:seed = 424242 same site, tab 1 cc9159d5dd44dc0e same site, tab 2 cc9159d5dd44dc0e equal: True (expected: equal) a different site 425ea3469ee3f27c equal: False (expected: not equal) Same profile, same seed, relaunched launch 1 cc9159d5dd44dc0e launch 2 57f921e26a94bcdc launch 3 abcf3e69880a54fe all equal: False (expected: equal, since the seed is fixed) Per-context API in this build window.setCanvasSeed undefined ``` The first block is correct behaviour: stable per site within a session, different across sites. Only the seed is the issue. ## Scope, for the record Since I had to measure this precisely, in case it saves you time: | Surface | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | `toDataURL()` / `toBlob()`, **2D** context | randomised per site, per session | | `toDataURL()`, **WebGL** context | randomised the same way | | `getImageData()` | stable | | `readPixels()` | stable | | `measureText()` | stable | So it is image export that is randomised, from either context type. ## What we do instead For completeness, so this does not read as a blocker: launching with `privacy.baselineFingerprintingProtection = false` disables the randomisation, and combined with a pinned `fonts:spacing_seed` the canvas becomes reproducible across launches. Text-bearing canvases need that second part — that is what misled me at first, since the font seed masked the pref's effect. That workaround costs cross-site unlinkability: the canvas becomes identical everywhere. For one long-lived account per profile that is the right trade and matches what a real machine does, so we will expose it as a per-profile setting rather than a default. A working `canvas:seed` would be strictly better than the pref, because it would give each profile its own canvas value instead of one shared true render — which is why the report is still worth making. ## Offer Happy to write the patch if you can point at where the export randomisation is applied; I could not find it from the repository alone and would rather not guess at C++ I cannot build and test here. I can also verify any build against the reproduction above on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 and report back. If the intended behaviour is that `canvas:seed` is reserved for the unreleased per-context work, feel free to close this — it would be worth a note in the property manifest either way, since the Python layer emits it today. ### Version: ``` Python Packages Camoufox v0.5.4 Browserforge v1.2.4 Apify Fingerprints v0.15.0 Playwright v1.60.0 Browser Active official/stable Current browser v152.0.4-beta.28 ``` Host: macOS 15 arm64. Also reproduced on Linux x86_64.

issues.title: add_init_script() no longer reaches the page world in beta.29, silently
issues.body:
### Describe the bug:

Since the isolated-world change in #707, `add_init_script()` only ever patches the isolated world. Any script installed that way — fingerprint spoofing, API patching, anything meant for the site — stops reaching page script.

`page.evaluate()` has the `mw:` escape hatch for this. Init scripts do not, and the two facts together make the failure silent.

Measured on the shipped `152.0.4-beta.29` Linux x86_64 build, A/B'd against `152.0.4-beta.28` on the same machine. The probe is a page served over local HTTP that hashes its own canvas from an inline `<script>` and writes the result to `document.title` — i.e. it measures what a *site* sees, not what automation sees.

| | init script reaches the page | profile A | profile B | A with no script |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| beta.28 | yes | `935f6c78` | `528b6cdb` | `5bf14e69` |
| beta.29 | **no** | `5bf14e69` | `5bf14e69` | `5bf14e69` |

Under beta.29 all three readings collapse onto the host's own rendering. Two profiles with different noise seeds hand a site the identical canvas.

Three things make this worse than a plain regression:

1. **The usual probe cannot see it.** Reading the same value back through `page.evaluate()` still returns two different, properly noised hashes — that is the world the init script landed in. Our browser test suite passed in full on a build that had stopped spoofing anything a site could observe.
2. **`mw:` in an init script is silently accepted.** Playwright wraps every `add_init_script` body in `(() => { ... })()`, so the prefix ends up *inside* the wrapper, where it parses as a label statement. No error, no effect.
3. **It is the failure mode a spoofing tool can least afford.** Nothing downstream can tell. Init scripts reach `ExecutionContext.evaluateScriptSafely()` (`FrameTree.js:660`), whose `catch` writes to `dump()` and returns — so even a throwing script surfaces nothing to the client. There is no exception, no warning, and every automation-side check keeps reporting success.

I'd suggest either wiring `mw:` through the init-script path, or — if init scripts are meant to stay isolated by design — rejecting the prefix loudly there, so it fails at call time instead of silently.

Adjacent but not the same: #733 reports globals leaking *into* the main world in 0.6.0. This is the opposite direction.

### Screenshots:

Not applicable — the measurements are in the table above.

### To Reproduce:

Serve a page that hashes its canvas in an inline `<script>` and writes it to `document.title`:

```html
<!doctype html><meta charset="utf-8"><body><script>
  const h = (t) => { let x = 5381;
    for (let i = 0; i < t.length; i++) x = ((x * 33) ^ t.charCodeAt(i)) >>> 0;
    return x.toString(16); };
  const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = 200; c.height = 50;
  const x = c.getContext('2d'); x.textBaseline = 'top'; x.font = '14px Arial';
  x.fillStyle = '#f60'; x.fillRect(0, 0, 100, 25);
  x.fillStyle = '#069'; x.fillText('probe', 2, 15);
  document.title = h(c.toDataURL()) + '|' + (window.__marker || 'absent');
</script></body>
```

Then:

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import NewBrowser
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

with sync_playwright() as pw:
    ctx = NewBrowser(pw, from_options=options, persistent_context=True)
    ctx.add_init_script("window.__marker = 'present';")   # plus any canvas patch
    page = ctx.new_page()
    page.goto(url, wait_until="load")
    print(page.title())
```

On beta.28 the title reports `present`. On beta.29 it reports `absent`, and the canvas hash is the host's, unchanged by whatever the init script did.

Prefixing the init script with `"mw:"` changes nothing either way, with or without `main_world_eval=True`.

<details>
<summary>What I tried, and why I am not sending it as a PR</summary>

`evaluateScriptSafely()` is the only path init scripts take — `FrameTree.js:660` runs it over `world._scriptsToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, per world, on `_onGlobalObjectCleared`. Teaching it the prefix — allowing for Playwright's wrapper — does restore the behaviour: the same probe then reads two distinct noised hashes.

The default world is the right place for it: `_createIsolatedContext()` gives its twin only to the unnamed world (`FrameTree.js:594`), which is exactly the one init scripts land in.

But it is **not reliable**. Over eight consecutive launches, two still rendered the host canvas. Same code, same profile: a race, not a logic error.

`mainWorldContext()` builds its `ExecutionContext` lazily from `_mainWorldGlobal`, which `_createIsolatedContext()` sets from `this.domWindow()`. When init scripts run, that global is occasionally not the one the document ends up with, and `executeInGlobal` either throws (swallowed by the surrounding `catch`) or writes into a global nobody reads.

Building the main-world twin eagerly, alongside the default world in `_createIsolatedContext()`, would tie it to the right document. I did not send that as a patch because the lazy build is commented as deliberate ("keeps the page's own global out of the debuggee set entirely for sessions that never use `mw:`"), and I cannot tell what eager creation costs elsewhere. That call is yours.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Workaround, for anyone hitting this</summary>

A content script declared in the main world does not go through Juggler at all, and works identically on both versions. Load it as a temporary extension:

```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "spoof",
  "version": "1.0",
  "browser_specific_settings": { "gecko": { "id": "spoof@example" } },
  "content_scripts": [{
    "matches": ["<all_urls>"],
    "js": ["spoof.js"],
    "run_at": "document_start",
    "all_frames": true,
    "world": "MAIN",
    "match_about_blank": true,
    "match_origin_as_fallback": true
  }]
}
```

then pass its directory via `addons=[...]`.

`match_about_blank` and `match_origin_as_fallback` matter: without them the inherited frames (`about:blank`, `blob:`, `srcdoc`) are missed, which is worse than no spoofing — the parent page is patched and the child frame is not.

Measured page-side under beta.29, this adds no observable surface: no extra own-property on `window`, `chrome` and `browser` both still `undefined`, `toDataURL.toString()` still `[native code]`. No `web_accessible_resources` is declared, which is what would expose the extension's internal UUID to the page.

</details>

### Version:

```
Python Packages
  Camoufox                    v0.5.5
  Browserforge                v1.2.4
  Apify Fingerprints          v0.15.0
  Playwright                  v1.60.0
Browser
  Camoufox                    v152.0.4-beta.29 (also tested against beta.28)
```

Linux x86_64.

issues.title: Juggler Protocol Rejects isMobile context prop from Playwright v1.62.1 in Browser.setDefaultViewport
issues.body:
### Describe the bug:

Newer Playwright versions send an `isMobile` property as part of the `Browser.setDefaultViewport` request https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/41179. Camoufox's Juggler protocol currently rejects this property because it is not defined in the protocol schema.

Error:

```text
browser.newContext: Protocol error (Browser.setDefaultViewport):
Found property "<root>.viewport.isMobile" - false which is not described in this scheme
```

The validation appears to originate from https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/main/additions/juggler/protocol/PrimitiveTypes.js#L99, where unknown properties are rejected.

Playwright is sending:

```json
{
  "viewportSize": {
    "width": 1280,
    "height": 720
  },
  "deviceScaleFactor": 1,
  "isMobile": false
}
```

This can happen even when `isMobile` is not explicitly specified by the user.

It appears that the Camoufox Juggler schema needs to be updated to recognize `isMobile`, or otherwise ignore it if Camoufox does not use the property.

### Screenshots:

Not applicable. The protocol error is included above.

### To Reproduce:

```javascript
newContext({
  viewport: {
    width: 1280,
    height: 720
  }
});
```

With the affected Playwright/Camoufox versions, this results in the `Browser.setDefaultViewport` protocol error above.

### Version:

Camoufox:

```text
$ python -m camoufox version
v152.0.4-beta.28
```

Playwright:

```text
$ npx playwright --version
v1.62.1
```

issues.title: Fingerprint cross-property inconsistency — synthetic BrowserForge fingerprints detectable as masking
issues.body:
### Describe the bug:

When using BrowserForge synthetic fingerprint generation (the default path in `generate_context_fingerprint()`), individual fingerprint properties are generated independently — BrowserForge provides navigator/screen, then fonts, voices, WebGL vendor/renderer, and seeds are added separately. This creates fingerprints where the combination of properties never exists on any real device, which fingerprint consistency detectors (Pixelscan, Fingerprint.com) can identify as "masking."

**Specifically:** The WebGL vendor/renderer is sampled from `webgl.py` independently of the BrowserForge screen resolution and navigator platform. The font subset is generated from the OS font list independently of the GPU profile. A real device with a specific GPU (e.g., Intel Iris Xe) ships with specific screen resolutions and a specific font set — the synthetic generation doesn't enforce this correlation.

**Evidence from testing:** Running Camoufox v152.0.4-beta.28 (headed via Xvfb, no proxy, residential IP) against the Pixelscan fingerprint check:

- Browser: Firefox 152.0 on Ubuntu — ✅ (correctly spoofed)
- Location: Australia / Mango Hill — ✅ (GeoIP matched)
- Proxy: No proxy detected — ✅
- Bot check: No automated behavior detected — ✅
- **Fingerprint: Masking detected** — ❌ ("Your Browser Fingerprint is inconsistent")

The browser integrity, location, proxy, and bot detection checks all pass. Only fingerprint consistency fails — indicating the spoofed properties don't form a coherent device profile.

**Note:** This affects the BrowserForge synthetic path. The bundled `fingerprint-presets.json` and `fingerprint-presets-v150.json` presets (from real devices) should be internally consistent already.

### Screenshots:

Pixelscan results showing "Masking detected" with all other checks passing:

![pixelscan-fingerprint-masking](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/pixelscan-fingerprint-masking.png)

### To Reproduce:

1. Launch Camoufox v152.0.4-beta.28 with default BrowserForge fingerprint generation (no preset)
2. Navigate to `https://pixelscan.net/fingerprint-check`
3. Observe "Masking detected" on the Fingerprint card while Browser, Location, Proxy, and Bot check all pass

```python
from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless="virtual") as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("https://pixelscan.net/fingerprint-check")
    page.wait_for_timeout(30000)
    page.screenshot(path="pixelscan.png")
```

### Version:

```
Browser: v152.0.4-beta.28
BrowserForge: v1.2.4
OS: Linux x86_64 (headed via Xvfb :99, 1920x1080x24)
```

### Proposed solution

Add a consistency validation step in `generate_context_fingerprint()` (Python layer, `pythonlib/camoufox/fingerprints.py`) that ensures cross-property coherence when using BrowserForge synthetic generation:

1. **WebGL ↔ screen resolution:** When sampling WebGL vendor/renderer from `webgl.py`, restrict to GPU profiles that are commonly paired with the BrowserForge screen resolution (e.g., a 1366x768 screen shouldn't claim a high-end discrete GPU)
2. **WebGL ↔ OS platform:** Already partially handled (OS map in the WebGL sampling), but could be tighter
3. **Fonts ↔ OS:** Already handled via `_generate_random_font_subset(os_name)`, but marker font injection should match the claimed platform
4. **Voices ↔ OS:** Already handled via `_generate_random_voice_subset(os_name)`

The main gap is #1 — the WebGL profile and screen resolution are independently sampled and can form combinations that don't exist on real hardware. A lookup table mapping GPU profiles to common screen resolutions would close this.

This is a Python-only change in `fingerprints.py` — no C++/browser patch needed.

issues.title: Python voices config does not match browser schema and exposes host voices
issues.body:
The Python wrapper emits `voices` as strings, but Camoufox browser `v152.0.4-beta.28` expects complete voice objects. The browser skips the string entries and can expose the Linux host's native voices.

Related fingerprint-coherence discussion: https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/issues/729

## Environment

- Camoufox browser `v152.0.4-beta.28`
- `cloverlabs-camoufox==0.6.0`
- BrowserForge `1.2.4`
- Headed browser under Xvfb
- Linux host

## Python behavior

The bundled `voices.json` entries use a `Name:locale:type` representation.

The Python wrapper:

1. Loads those entries.
2. Keeps only the name.
3. Generates `List[str]`.
4. Places that list in `config["voices"]`.

The fallback path can place the original string records in the same property. Therefore, one property can receive two string formats.

The browser's `properties.json` declares only:

```json
{ "property": "voices", "type": "array" }
```

The Python validator checks that the value is a list. It cannot validate the element schema.

## Browser behavior

The browser source for this build requires every `voices` element to contain:

```json
{
  "lang": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "voiceUri": "string",
  "isDefault": true,
  "isLocalService": true
}
```

The parser skips a bare string or an incomplete object.

The build also supports:

```text
voices:blockIfNotDefined
```

When that option is false or absent, native host voices can still register.

## Reproduction

A bundled macOS real-device preset was launched on a Linux host.

With the wrapper-generated string configuration:

- The configured entries were skipped.
- `speechSynthesis.getVoices()` exposed 14,805 host Linux voices.

With structured objects and `voices:blockIfNotDefined=true`:

- The browser exposed only the intended configured voices.
- The host voice leak was removed.

No voice names, IP addresses, proxy details, or private infrastructure values are included here.

A Python-only shape check also demonstrates the mismatch:

```python
config = from_preset(preset, "152")
assert isinstance(config["voices"], list)
assert all(isinstance(voice, str) for voice in config["voices"])
```

## Expected behavior

- The Python package and browser must use one documented voice element schema.
- The Python package must preserve the locale and voice type needed to build that schema.
- Invalid elements must fail validation before browser launch.
- The browser must define whether an empty configured list blocks or permits native voices.
- A valid configured list must not expose unconfigured host voices.
- Wrapper/browser compatibility data must prevent installation of a pair with incompatible configuration schemas.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- `from_preset` emits the documented voice object format.
- Every object contains `lang`, `name`, `voiceUri`, `isDefault`, and `isLocalService`.
- Element-level validation rejects strings and incomplete objects.
- A Linux-hosted browser using a macOS preset exposes no Linux host voices.
- Tests cover a valid list, an invalid string, an incomplete object, and an empty list.
- The expected interaction with `voices:blockIfNotDefined` is documented and tested.
- The supported Python-package/browser matrix includes the configuration-schema version.

This issue is separate from #729 because it has a specific type mismatch, reproduction, and acceptance boundary. The two issues are related because the leaked host voices make the resulting device profile internally inconsistent.

issues.title: Camoufox crashes with SIGSEGV under gVisor sandboxes — wasm_rt_syscall_set_segue_base / ARCH_SET_GS unsupported
issues.body:
## Summary

Camoufox crashes with `SIGSEGV` a few seconds after launch when run inside a
[gVisor](https://gvisor.dev/)-sandboxed container (e.g. [Modal](https://modal.com/)
functions, Google Cloud Run, GKE Sandbox/GKE Autopilot). The crash is not
specific to Camoufox's own code — it's Firefox 136+'s WASM sandbox
(RLBox/wasm2c) requiring `arch_prctl(ARCH_SET_GS, ...)`, a syscall gVisor
does not implement ([google/gvisor#11567](https://github.com/google/gvisor/issues/11567)).
Filing here since Camoufox pins/ships that Firefox base and this will bite
anyone trying to deploy Camoufox on gVisor-backed serverless platforms.

## Environment

- camoufox-js: `0.12.0`
- playwright: `1.60.0`
- Base image: `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.60.0-noble`
- Host: Modal (gVisor-sandboxed container runtime), x86_64
- Launch options: `{ headless: true, geoip: true }` via `launchOptions()` from `camoufox-js`

## Repro

```js
import { launchOptions } from 'camoufox-js';
import { firefox } from 'playwright';

const opts = await launchOptions({ headless: true, geoip: true });
const browser = await firefox.launch(opts);
browser.on('disconnected', () => console.log('disconnected'));
// crashes within ~3s of launch, before any page is opened
```

## Observed (with `DEBUG=pw:browser`)

```
pw:browser <launching> /opt/camoufox/camoufox-bin -no-remote -headless -profile ... -juggler-pipe -silent
pw:browser <launched> pid=38
pw:browser [pid=38][err] *** You are running in headless mode.
pw:browser [pid=38][out] [GFX1-]: FireTestProcess failed: Failed to spawn child process "/opt/camoufox/glxtest" (No such file or directory)
pw:browser [pid=38][err] JavaScript warning: resource://services-settings/Utils.sys.mjs, line 119: unreachable code after return statement
pw:browser [pid=38][out] Juggler listening to the pipe
pw:browser [pid=38][err] wasm_rt_syscall_set_segue_base error: Invalid argument
pw:browser [pid=38][err] Redirecting call to abort() to mozalloc_abort
pw:browser [pid=38] <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGSEGV>
```

## What I tried

- Setting `MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1` in the launched process's env
  (confirmed via `opts.env.MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX` that it does reach
  the child process) — no effect. This makes sense in hindsight: this is
  the WASM/RLBox sandbox, not the OS-level content-process sandbox that env
  var controls.
- No firefox_user_pref or launch arg found that disables the WASM
  segue-based sandboxing at runtime.

## Question / ask

Is there a supported way to disable the WASM segue optimization (or the
RLBox-sandboxed libraries that trigger it) at runtime or launch-option time,
so Camoufox can run under gVisor-based sandboxes until gVisor implements
`ARCH_SET_GS`? If there's a Firefox pref or build flag for this already,
happy to test and report back — a `launchOptions()` flag would make this a
clean workaround for anyone deploying to gVisor-backed platforms (Modal,
Cloud Run, GKE Sandbox).

Reference: https://github.com/google/gvisor/issues/11567
issues.display_title: Camoufox crashes with SIGSEGV under gVisor sandboxes — wasm_rt_syscall_set_segue_base / ARCH_SET_GS unsupported

issues.title: macOS: headed Camoufox activates itself (steals key/mouse focus) at window show — even with Playwright's '-foreground' launch flag removed
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, every headed Camoufox launch brings its window to the very front and takes keyboard AND mouse focus from whatever app the user is working in. This makes unattended automation on a machine someone is actively using very painful (we run one fresh Camoufox per scraped URL — each launch interrupts the user).

We isolated it past the usual suspect: Playwright's Firefox launcher normally passes the '-foreground' CLI flag (launch-time activation). We removed it via `ignore_default_args=["-foreground"]` (passed through camoufox's launch_options to firefox.launch) and verified via `ps` that the real spawned process runs WITHOUT it:

```
camoufox -no-remote -wait-for-browser -profile <tmp> -juggler-pipe -silent
```

The focus steal still happens — but NOT at launch: measured with a 0.25s AppleScript poll of AXMain on the Camoufox process, the window becomes key at ~t=3.6s and STAYS key for ~3s, which lines up with browser-window creation/first show (new_page/goto), not process start. So something in the window-show path performs an explicit self-activation.

For comparison, the Playwright team states (microsoft/playwright#41306) that stock headed Firefox no longer steals focus once '-foreground' is dropped — so this looks specific to the Camoufox build (window sizing/positioning patches or theming performing an explicit raise/activate on show?).

An `LSUIElement=true` Info.plist patch on the .app bundle does not help either — consistent with an explicit activation call overriding the passive accessory policy (the Dock icon also still appears on these direct-binary launches).

### To Reproduce

```python
from camoufox.async_api import AsyncCamoufox
# ignore_default_args passes through to playwright.firefox.launch
async with AsyncCamoufox(headless=False, os="macos", ignore_default_args=["-foreground"]) as browser:
    page = await browser.new_page()
    await page.goto("https://example.com")
```
Focus another app before the window appears — Camoufox raises itself above it and takes key focus at window show.

### Expected

A way to launch headed Camoufox on macOS without it activating itself — e.g. respect the '-foreground'-absent launch by not self-activating on first window show, or a config/pref to suppress the raise (the analog of what makes stock headed Firefox background-friendly).

### Environment
- Camoufox 152.0.4-beta.28 (official, ~/Library/Caches/camoufox), python lib via Playwright bundled driver
- macOS arm64
- Workaround we run today: an external watchdog that re-activates the previously focused app whenever Camoufox becomes key — bounds the steal to a sub-second flicker, but a real fix needs to be in the browser.
issues.display_title: macOS: headed Camoufox activates itself (steals key/mouse focus) at window show — even with Playwright's '-foreground' launch flag removed

issues.title: Docker linux/arm64 build OOM-killed during link (+ missing ccache, no .dockerignore)
issues.body:
## Bug report

Building for **linux/arm64** via the documented Docker path fails, and a couple of related Docker-build rough edges remain. Verified against current `main` (`152.0.4-beta.28`).

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
docker build -t camoufox-builder .
docker run -v "$(pwd)/dist:/app/dist" camoufox-builder --target linux --arch arm64
```

### 1. arm64 build gets OOM-killed during the link (primary)

**Expected:** the build completes and produces `camoufox-*-lin.arm64.zip`.

**Actual:** the compile runs but the process is `SIGKILL`ed (OOM) at the memory-heavy link stage — the `gkrust` fat-LTO staticlib (`-Clto -Cdebuginfo=2 -Ccodegen-units=1`) and the `libxul` link peak past available RAM on arm64. `assets/linux.mozconfig` sets no debug-symbol level, so debug info is generated and the link blows the memory ceiling.

**Fix:** add `ac_add_options --disable-debug-symbols` to `assets/linux.mozconfig`. Distribution builds don't ship symbols anyway; this keeps the link under the RAM ceiling and also shrinks the binary. (With this, a full `linux/arm64` build completes and packages successfully.)

### 2. Dockerfile never installs `ccache`

`assets/base.mozconfig` now enables ccache conditionally (`if command -v ccache …`), but the `Dockerfile`'s `apt-get install` list has no `ccache`, so **every Docker build runs cold** — the conditional is always false in-image. Adding `ccache` to the Dockerfile package list restores incremental caching (and pairs well with mounting a cache volume at `CCACHE_DIR`).

### 3. No `.dockerignore` (build-context hygiene)

With no `.dockerignore`, `COPY . /app` ships the host `.git`, `dist/` (hundreds of MB), any extracted `camoufox-*/` source tree, and `node_modules/` into the build context — slow and bloated. A small `.dockerignore` excluding those trims the context substantially.

> Note: the earlier "source tree wiped mid-build" failure (where `patch.py`'s `git clean -fdx` walked up to the `/app` git work tree created by `COPY . /app`) is already mitigated on `main` by the `reset_to_unpatched()` guard (`if not os.path.exists('.git'): return`). So `.dockerignore` here is hygiene, not a correctness fix.

### Environment

- Host: Apple Silicon (arm64), Docker Desktop — native `linux/arm64`, no emulation.
- Target: `--target linux --arch arm64`, Camoufox `152.0.4-beta.28`.

### Scope

Items 1–3 are small, self-contained Docker/build changes. Item 1 is the actual build blocker for arm64; 2 and 3 are build-speed / hygiene improvements. Happy to open a PR.
issues.display_title: Docker linux/arm64 build OOM-killed during link (+ missing ccache, no .dockerignore)

issues.title: camoufox.exe fails to launch on Windows: SxS manifest declares mozglue as win32 assembly dependency
issues.body:
```
## Environment
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26100 (x64)
- Camoufox binary: 135.0.1-beta.24
- Python camoufox package
- Error: `spawn UNKNOWN` from Playwright when launching camoufox.exe

## Problem

`camoufox.exe` fails to start on Windows. The process exits immediately
with no output. Windows Application Event Log shows:

> Fehler beim Generieren des Aktivierungskontextes für "camoufox.exe".
> Die abhängige Assemblierung "mozglue,language="*",type="win32",
> version="1.0.0.0"" konnte nicht gefunden werden.

(English: "Error generating activation context. The dependent assembly
'mozglue' could not be found.")

## Root Cause

The embedded XML manifest inside `camoufox.exe` declares `mozglue.dll`
as a **Windows SxS (Side-by-Side) assembly dependency**:

```xml
<dependency>
  <dependentAssembly>
    <assemblyIdentity
      type="win32"
      name="mozglue"
      version="1.0.0.0"
      language="*"
    />
  </dependentAssembly>
</dependency>
```

This is incorrect. SxS is for shared system assemblies (e.g. Microsoft.Windows.Common-Controls). For a private DLL bundled in the same directory, the correct declaration is a direct ```<file>``` reference:

```<file name="mozglue.dll" />```

Windows tries to resolve mozglue from C:\Windows\WinSxS\ and as a registered private assembly — both fail — so the activation context cannot be created and the process never starts.

Note: external .manifest file overrides do NOT fix this because Windows merges them with the embedded manifest rather than replacing it.

## Workaround
Patch the embedded manifest in camoufox.exe directly — replace the <dependency>...</dependency> block (291 bytes) with spaces in-place to preserve file size. The resulting manifest is valid XML and Windows loads mozglue.dll from the exe directory without SxS lookup.

```
import shutil
src = r'path\to\camoufox.exe'
shutil.copy2(src, src + '.bak')

with open(src, 'rb') as f:
    data = bytearray(f.read())

search = (
    b'<dependency>\n        <dependentAssembly>\n'
    b'                <assemblyIdentity\n'
    b'                        type="win32"\n'
    b'                        name="mozglue"\n'
    b'                        version="1.0.0.0"\n'
    b'                        language="*"\n'
    b'                />\n        </dependentAssembly>\n</dependency>'
)
idx = data.find(search)
if idx >= 0:
    data[idx:idx+len(search)] = b' ' * len(search)
    with open(src, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(data)
    print('Patched')
```

## Fix
The proper fix is to change the manifest in the build system so mozglue is declared as ```<file name="mozglue.dll" />``` instead of a ```<dependency>``` block. This matches how standard Firefox builds handle private DLLs.

Related: [#622](https://github.com/e-orlov/oneglanse/issues/622) (Windows Support)
issues.display_title: camoufox.exe fails to launch on Windows: SxS manifest declares mozglue as win32 assembly dependency

issues.title: Headed mode on Windows: visual artifacts and stale rendering when resizing the window during interactive use
issues.body:
## User experience

A human operator drives a headed Camoufox window interactively (manual login flows, OAuth consent screens). While resizing the OS window, the right-hand side of the viewport shows persistent rendering artifacts, and page content intermittently fails to redraw after navigation or redirect — the page appears stalled until another interaction forces a repaint. The workflow breaks because the operator cannot trust what is rendered while adjusting the window mid-flow.

Observed on Windows 10 (10.0.26100), Camoufox v0.5.5 (Python package), browser build official/stable v152.0.4-beta.28 (Firefox 152), launched with `headless=False, humanize=True` via `sync_api`.

## Reproduction

1. Launch a headed session:
   ```python
   from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox
   with Camoufox(headless=False, humanize=True) as browser:
       page = browser.new_page()
       page.goto("https://vercel.com/login", wait_until="domcontentloaded")
       input()  # keep window open; resize it by dragging edges now
   ```
2. Drag-resize the window repeatedly by its right edge.
3. Observe artifacts along the resized edge; then navigate to a URL that redirects (e.g. an OAuth provider) and watch whether the new page paints without further input.

## Expected behavior

Resizing repaints cleanly with no residual artifacts, and navigations/redirects paint the new document promptly without requiring additional user input.

## Actual behavior

- Stale pixels / torn strips remain visible along the right-hand side of the viewport while dragging to resize.
- After redirects (observed crossing from vercel.com into accounts.google.com), the interstitial sometimes does not paint; content appears frozen until a subsequent event triggers compositing.

## Impact

Any headed, human-in-the-loop flow (OAuth logins, consent screens) on Windows is affected. Headless automation does not surface this because there is no interactive resize. Current workaround: avoid resizing mid-flow, or relaunch; forcing software WebRender (`gfx.webrender.software=true`) is expected to mitigate but trades CPU for GPU compositing.

## Source references

This matches a long-standing class of Firefox WebRender compositor bugs on Windows:
- [Bugzilla #1578330](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1578330) — "[Windows] Glitches when resizing browser window with WebRender"; root cause was `GetBufferSize()` being called after `BeginFrame()` in `RenderCompositorANGLE`, mutating the buffer size mid-frame.
- [Bugzilla #1626116](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1626116) — stretched content when resizing under ANGLE-related WebRender paths on Windows.
- [Bugzilla #2027221](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2027221) — WebRender compositor defect in Firefox 149 (dirty-rect/device-size handling), fixed in Firefox ~150; Camoufox v152 should include that specific fix, which suggests either a regression in the 152 line or an interaction with Camoufox's patched build.

Relevant Camoufox-side code paths (hypothesis only): window sizing/viewport sync logic around [`pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py`](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/dbd511b962/pythonlib/camoufox/utils.py) (launch options → Firefox window args) and the addons that patch window/screen dimensions at [`pythonlib/camoufox/addons/`](https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/blob/dbd511b962/pythonlib/camoufox/addons/). The spoofed screen-size injection may interact badly with real OS resize events in headed mode.

## Suggested acceptance criteria

- Drag-resizing a headed window on Windows 10/11 leaves no stale strips or torn regions.
- A cross-origin redirect in a headed window paints the new document within normal frame timing without requiring extra input.
- Regression check: repeat the repro above on integrated and discrete GPUs.

## Related

- #192 — window size incorrect with persistent context (related sizing behavior, different symptom: wrong initial size rather than live-resize artifacts)
- #118, #532, #348 — earlier window-size reports
- #514 — Windows-specific graphics-stack findings (ANGLE/GPU strings) that motivated looking at the compositor path
issues.display_title: Headed mode on Windows: visual artifacts and stale rendering when resizing the window during interactive use

issues.title: Playwright globals leak into the page's main world in 0.6.0 (detected by hcaptcha)
issues.body:
With cloverlabs-camoufox[geoip]==0.6.0, Playwright identifiers are visible on window in the page's main world, where any page script can enumerate them. Upstream camoufox==0.4.11 exposes none.

Repro (a <script> tag always runs in the main world, so it measures what the page sees regardless of which world page.evaluate targets):

from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

SNIPPET = """
  const n = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(window);
  document.title = JSON.stringify(n.filter(k => /playwright|pwInit|puppeteer|juggler|cdc_/i.test(k)));
"""

with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    page.goto("https://example.com")
    page.add_script_tag(content=SNIPPET)
    print(page.title())


Two separate things: __pwInitScripts / __playwright_builtins__ look new in Playwright 1.52 (stripping predates them), while __playwright__binding__ is hidden by 0.4.11 and not by 0.6.0 — a regression independent of the driver.

Impact: trivially detectable by Object.getOwnPropertyNames(window) scans. On an hCaptcha-protected workload, 0.4.11 + pw1.49.1 got 19/20 tokens accepted; 0.6.0 + pw1.52 got 3/20, same sites and network, alternating runs. Linux, headless, no proxy/addons/custom prefs; note the clean run used the newer browser build (152.0.4-beta.29 vs 150.0.2-alpha.26), so it isn't a browser-version effect.

Secondary: main_world_eval appears to be a no-op on 0.6.0 — page.evaluate sees 951 window properties either way, vs 77 (isolated world) on 0.4.11.

issues.title: Deterministic Hardware Fingerprinting (Seed Persistence) for Session Reuse
issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

**The Problem:**
Currently, `persistent_context=True` successfully persists storage states (Cookies, LocalStorage), but it does **not** persist the randomization seeds used for hardware fingerprinting.

Every time the browser instance is restarted (even with the same `user_data_dir`), Camoufox regenerates:
1.  **Canvas/WebGL/Audio Noise Seeds:** Causing the "Fingerprint ID" / "VisitorID" to change completely.
2.  **Hardware Concurrency:** The CPU core count reported by `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` drifts randomly (e.g., 16 -> 12 -> 14).
3.  **GPU Renderer Strings:** Often switch between different mocked vendors.

**The Impact:**
For automation workflows requiring long-term session reuse, this behavior is problematic. Anti-fraud systems interpret this as "Session Hijacking" because the user identity (Cookies) remains the same, but the device characteristics (Hardware Fingerprint) abruptly change.

## Describe the solution you'd like

I request a mechanism to make the hardware fingerprint **deterministic** based on the profile data.

**Proposed Logic:**
1.  When a `user_data_dir` is initialized, generate the randomization seeds (Canvas/WebGL noise, Hardware Concurrency value, etc.) once.
2.  Save these seeds/configurations into a file within the `user_data_dir` (e.g., `fingerprint_config.json` or inside `user.js`).
3.  On subsequent launches pointing to this directory, **load these existing seeds** instead of generating new random ones.

This would ensure that a specific profile always "looks" like the exact same device, enabling true session persistence.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1.  **Commercial Anti-detect Browsers + Playwright/Rebrowser:**
    * *Failure:* We attempted to automate popular commercial fingerprint browsers using Playwright and Rebrowser patches. However, the external CDP connection often triggers **Cloudflare** checks immediately. Camoufox's internal integration proves to be much stealthier against Cloudflare, which is why we prefer sticking with Camoufox if the persistence issue can be solved.
2.  **JS Injection (e.g., `page.add_init_script`):**
    * *Limitation:* This fails to cover **Web Workers**, which are commonly used by advanced fingerprinting libraries to detect inconsistencies.
3.  **Keeping the browser open indefinitely:**
    * *Limitation:* Not scalable for resource-constrained environments.

## Additional context

* **OS:** Linux / Windows
* **Use Case:** RPA with strict consistency requirements.
issues.display_title: Deterministic Hardware Fingerprinting (Seed Persistence) for Session Reuse

issues.title: Spoof navigator.maxTouchPoints from config
issues.body:
## Feature request

### Use case

`navigator.maxTouchPoints` is already a recognized config property — `settings/properties.json` declares `{ "property": "navigator.maxTouchPoints", "type": "uint" }` — but **nothing reads it**. It is validated and then silently ignored, so it always reports `0` on a desktop build regardless of what the config sets.

Under a Firefox-for-Android user agent this is a mobile-detection tell: a real phone reports `maxTouchPoints = 5`, but Camoufox reports `0`. A desktop build has no touch digitizer, and Firefox's RFP path only ever *collapses* the value to `0` (`MaxTouchPointsCollapse`) — there is no path to a phone value without an explicit override.

Verified live: setting `navigator.maxTouchPoints` in `CAMOU_CONFIG` currently has no effect (stays `0`); disabling the RFP collapse target and enabling touch-events prefs also has no effect, because the underlying host value is genuinely `0`.

### Why it's useful

`maxTouchPoints` is the one touch signal that needs a browser-level override. The rest of the mobile touch surface (touch events, `pointer: coarse`, `hover: none`) is already reachable via Playwright `hasTouch`, so honouring the existing config property closes the remaining gap and makes a consistent Android fingerprint possible.

### Proposed change

Read the already-declared config property in `Navigator::MaxTouchPoints` via the standard `MaskConfig` early-return, matching how every other navigator/screen property is spoofed. No schema change required.
issues.display_title: Spoof navigator.maxTouchPoints from config
